signature: SUBROUTINE DHSEQR( JOB, COMPZ, N, ILO, IHI, H, LDH, WR, WI, Z,

params.name: job
params.reference:
-   `= 'E'`: compute eigenvalues only;
-   `= 'S'`: compute eigenvalues and the Schur form T.

params.name: compz
N
params.reference: The order of the matrix H. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: ihi
params.reference: It is assumed that H is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to DGEBAL, and then passed to ZGEHRD when the matrix output by DGEBAL is reduced to Hessenberg form. Otherwise `ILO` and `IHI` should be set to 1 and N respectively. If $N > 0$, then $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$. If $N = 0$, then `ILO = 1` and `IHI = 0`.

params.name: H
params.reference:
On entry, the upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if `INFO = 0` and `JOB = 'S'`, then H contains the upper quasi-triangular matrix T from the Schur decomposition (the Schur form); 2-by-2 diagonal blocks (corresponding to complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues) are returned in standard form, with $H(i,i) = H(i+1,i+1)$ and $H(i+1,i) \, H(i,i+1) < 0$. If `INFO = 0` and `JOB = 'E'`, the contents of H are unspecified on exit. (The output value of H when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)

Unlike earlier versions of DHSEQR, this subroutine may explicitly $H(i,j) = 0$ for $i > j$ and $j = 1$, 2, ... `ILO`-1 or $j = \mathrm{IHI}+1$, `IHI`+2, ... N.

params.name: ldh
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array H. $\mathrm{LDH} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: WI
params.reference: The real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. If two eigenvalues are computed as a complex conjugate pair, they are stored in consecutive elements of `WR` and `WI`, say the i-th and (i+1)th, with $\mathrm{WI}(i) > 0$ and $\mathrm{WI}(i+1) < 0$. If `JOB = 'S'`, the eigenvalues are stored in the same order as on the diagonal of the Schur form returned in H, with `WR(i) = H(i,i)` and, if `H(i:i+1,i:i+1)` is a 2-by-2 diagonal block, `WI(i) = sqrt(-H(i+1,i)*H(i,i+1))` and `WI(i+1) = -WI(i)`.

params.name: Z
params.reference: If `COMPZ = 'N'`, Z is not referenced. If `COMPZ = 'I'`, on entry Z need not be set and on exit, if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the orthogonal matrix Z of the Schur vectors of H. If `COMPZ = 'V'`, on entry Z must contain an N-by-N matrix Q, which is assumed to be equal to the unit matrix except for the submatrix `Z(ILO:IHI,ILO:IHI)`. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, Z contains $Q \, Z$. Normally Q is the orthogonal matrix generated by DORGHR after the call to DGEHRD which formed the Hessenberg matrix H. (The output value of Z when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Z. if `COMPZ = 'I'` or `COMPZ = 'V'`, then $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge \max (1,N)$. Otherwise, $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge 1$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns an estimate of the optimal value for `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,N)$ is sufficient and delivers very good and sometimes optimal performance. However, `LWORK` as large as $11 \, N$ may be required for optimal performance. A workspace query is recommended to determine the optimal workspace size.

If `LWORK = -1`, then DHSEQR does a workspace query. In this case, DHSEQR checks the input parameters and estimates the optimal workspace size for the given values of N, `ILO` and `IHI`. The estimate is returned in `WORK(1)`. No error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA. Neither H nor Z are accessed.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, DHSEQR failed to compute all of the eigenvalues.  Elements 1:ilo-1 and i+1:n of `WR` and `WI` contain those eigenvalues which have been successfully computed.  (Failures are rare.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `JOB = 'E'`, then on exit, the remaining unconverged eigenvalues are the eigen- values of the upper Hessenberg matrix rows and columns `ILO` through `INFO` of the final, output value of H.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `JOB = 'S'`, then on exit

```text
(*)  (initial value of H)*U  = U*(final value of H)
```

where U is an orthogonal matrix. The final value of H is upper Hessenberg and quasi-triangular in rows and columns `INFO`+1 through `IHI`.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'V'`, then on exit

(final value of Z) = (initial value of Z)\*U

where U is the orthogonal matrix in (\*) (regard- less of the value of `JOB`.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'I'`, then on exit

(final value of Z) = U

where U is the orthogonal matrix in (\*) (regard- less of the value of `JOB`.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'N'`, then Z is not accessed.

checks.js: ihi < min( ilo, N ) || ihi > N
